## The design

![Mockup](mockup.png)

Frames in the picture: **A1** the card with changes, **A2** the card with
nothing changed and nothing sliced, **B** the setup page. Top row light, bottom
row dark. Each frame is 320 px wide, the panel's minimum width
(`component.agentPane.minWidth`), which is the worst case for fitting text.

### The card in the chat (A1, A2)

The card keeps its header, state label, estimate area, attention block,
working and saved-chat behaviour exactly as they are. Only the lines between
the title and the estimate change, and the "Setup details" toggle becomes a
link.

| Line | Rule | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| Title | The chat's recorded purpose (`setupIntent`); otherwise the full process preset name. Unchanged from today. | Never. |
| Presets line | Process preset and first filament preset, each cut at the first `" @"`, joined with `" · "`; `+N` after the filament when there are more filament slots. When the title is already the process preset, show the filaments only. | Non-FFF printer: omit. |
| Change rows | The first two differences from the presets, as `label` and `display_change` text. Order in the next section. | No differences: one line, "No changes from presets". |
| Count note | "N more changes" when there are more than two, and "N objects with overrides" when any object on the active plate has overrides, joined with `" · "`. | Both zero: omit. |
| Estimate and everything below | Unchanged. | |
| View setup | Opens the setup page. Replaces the "Setup details" toggle. | Never. |

The card never expands. Remove the inline `Details` block and the dimming of
the thread (`thread-dimmed`) that went with it.

Why the presets line is cut and has no printer: measured over every preset
shipped in `resources/profiles`, three full names joined are about 64
characters at the median and the card fits about 45. Process and filament cut
at `" @"` are about 33 at the median and 44 at the 90th percentile. The cut is
a naming convention (97% of process and 88% of filament presets follow it); a
name without `" @"` is shown whole and ends in an ellipsis if it overflows.
Full names are always on the setup page.

### Order of the change rows

1. Differences the agent made, then differences the person made
   (`PresetDeltaInfo.origin`, which exists today).
2. Within each, newest first. This needs the setting's key on the change log
   (see step 4). Where no change-log entry exists for a difference, use
   OrcaSlicer's own settings order (`Preset::print_options()` and its filament
   and printer equivalents), process before filament before printer.

### The setup page (B)

It replaces the chat body, like the chat list does. The message box is hidden.
"Back" returns to the chat. Sections, each present only when it has content:

| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Header | The same label, state and title as the card. | As the card. |
| Presets | Printer, process, each filament slot, build plate, with full names. | `setupIdentity`, `printer.process`. All exist today. |
| Changed from presets · N | Grouped first by preset (its full name), then by "page · group" from OrcaSlicer's settings tabs, then one row per setting. | `presetDeltas`, extended in steps 2 and 3. |
| Objects on \<plate\> · N | One line per printable object. An object with overrides is a disclosure that opens to rows grouped by what the override is on ("Whole object", "\<name\> · modifier"). An object without any reads "Uses plate settings". | `appliedSetup.objects`, `appliedSetup.localOverrides`, extended in step 5. |
| Plates | One row per plate: name, "shown" on the active one, and its estimate or "Not sliced". | `plates[]`. Exists today. |

A saved chat's page is built from that chat's saved summary, never from the
live project, exactly as the card is today.

### What makes the lines change

The lines are not stored. The host re-sends the context on every workspace
change and again after a successful agent settings change or title update
(`AgentHost`'s workspace and tool-activity subscriptions), and the page
rebuilds from it. So:

- The presets line changes when a different process or filament preset is
  selected, the printer is switched, a preset is saved under a new name, or a
  project is opened.
- The change rows change when a setting is edited by hand or by the agent,
  put back to the preset's value, restored by undo or redo, when the preset is
  saved with the edits in it, or when a different preset is selected.
- Selecting or moving objects and slicing change only the estimate. Switching
  plates changes the object-override count and the estimate.

## Styling contract: tokens only, nothing freehand

The design system is `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, applied to the
page as CSS variables by `WebShared/tokens.ts` and `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts`.
Read "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before
touching any style. `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` fails the build on a literal
colour, radius or font in the stylesheet.

`mockup.html` was generated, not drawn: `make-mockup.py` writes the variables
from the token file with the same naming rules the page uses, includes
`AgentUI/src/styles.css` unedited, and adds the four new rules below. Running
it again reproduces the file byte for byte:

```bash
python3 make-mockup.py mockup.html <path to your checkout>
```

### Every element and the existing style it uses

| Element in the mockup | Existing class | Type role | Colour and shape tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card container | `.current-setup` | | `--surface-subtle`; `--radius-container` |
| Accent edge on a live card | `.current-setup--live` | | `--action-primary` |
| "Setup summary" / state | `.current-setup-header`, `-label`, `-state` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--action-primary` live, `--text-secondary` otherwise |
| Title | `.current-setup-title` | `--font-body-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Presets line, "No changes from presets", estimate sentence | `.current-setup-line` | `--font-label` | `--text-secondary` |
| A row: name left, value right | `.current-setup-rows`, `.current-setup-row` (`dt`, `dd`) | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` name, `--text-primary` value |
| Count note, "Uses plate settings" | `.current-setup-note` | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` |
| Time, material, plate | `.current-setup-metrics`, `-metric` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-primary`; icons `--text-secondary` at `--setup-card-icon-size` |
| Divider | `.current-setup-divider` | | `--border-subtle` |
| "View setup", "Compute estimates" | `.current-setup-link` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary`, `-hover`, `-pressed`; `--radius-standard` |
| Section heading ("Presets") | `.current-setup h3` inside `.current-setup-section` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary` |
| Preset name above its groups, object name | `.current-setup-object-name` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Object that opens | `.current-setup-disclosure` with `.jp-icon-chevron-down` / `-right` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary`; `--radius-standard`; icon `--button-icon-icon-size` |
| Page header bar | `.chat-header` | | `--surface-canvas`, `--border-subtle` |
| "Back" | `.printer-link-button.printer-back-link` with `.jp-icon-chevron-left` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary` |
| Area around the card | `.pinned-setup` | | `--surface-canvas` |

Icons are the existing `jp-icon-*` masks: `clock`, `package`, `grid-3x3`,
`chevron-left`, `chevron-down`, `chevron-right`. No new icon.

"Back" borrows a class named for the printer panel. Give the rule a neutral
name shared by both uses; do not copy its declarations into a second rule.

### The four rules this design adds

They are in `mockup.html` under "Rules this design adds". Each uses only
existing variables and spacing from the 4-to-48 scale. No new token is needed.

| New class | Purpose | Declarations that carry a token or scale value |
|---|---|---|
| `.current-setup-page` | The page's scrolling body. | `padding: 12px`; `background: var(--surface-canvas)`. The same two values as `.pinned-setup`. |
| `.current-setup-group` | "Others · Brim" caption above a run of rows. | `font: var(--font-metadata-bold)`; `color: var(--text-secondary)`; `padding-top: 4px`. The same role and colour as `.current-setup-sent`. |
| `.current-setup-row--change` | Keeps a change row on one line: the name truncates with an ellipsis, the value is never cut. | Layout only (`flex`, `min-width`, `overflow`, `max-width: 60%`). The full name goes in the `title` attribute. |
| `.current-setup-object-rows` | Indents an opened object's rows under its name. | `padding-left: 24px` (icon 16 + gap 8); `gap: 4px`. |

New class names must start with `current-setup-`. The `setup-*` prefix belongs
to the agent's setup screens, the stylesheet is global, and a clash there once
broke layout with every test passing.

### Deliberately not in the design

- **No "agent" / "you" badge on a row.** An earlier sketch had one. The
  design system has no badge or tag component, so drawing one would be
  freehand. Who made a change is carried by the order of the rows. Adding a
  badge is a design decision for Kenneth.
- **No new colour, type size or radius.** If you believe you need one, stop
  and ask. Do not add a token on your own for this work.

## Implementation steps

Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `architecture.md` and, before any edit
outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, `fork-stewardship.md`. Nothing below needs
a change to an OrcaSlicer-owned file; if you find one that does, stop and
report it with the reason.

1. **Apply `formatter.patch`.** Build and run `setting_display_tests`.
2. **Send differences for all three preset types.** In the workspace
   snapshot, call `preset_deltas_of` for the edited filament preset and the
   edited printer preset as well as the process preset. Add to each
   difference: which preset type it belongs to, that preset's name, and the
   `display_change` text. Keep the raw `preset` and `value` fields.
3. **Add the page and group of each setting.** Look each key up in
   OrcaSlicer's search index (`Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option`).
   **Warning:** when a key is not in the index, for example because the
   current user mode hides it, that function returns some other option
   instead of failing. Compare the returned option's key with the one you
   asked for, and send no page or group when they differ. Also check what it
   returns for per-filament keys, which the index stores with a `#0` suffix.
   This lookup has been read in the source but never run; verify it in the
   running app before building on it.
4. **Put the setting's key on the change log.** `WorkspaceEdit` and
   `ChangeInfo` carry a label, and labels are not unique (17 process labels
   are shared; "Outer wall" names four settings). Add the key as an optional
   field so the card can order differences newest first.
5. **Name every override.** For each entry in `local_overrides`, send the
   setting's label and `display_value` text. The card then stops using

   setting now has a name.
6. **Remove the fixed list.** Delete `kSetupKeys`, the `settings` array it

7. **Rebuild the card and add the page** to the rules and styles above. Add a
   view to `App.tsx`'s switch, hide the message box on it, and return to the
   chat on "Back", on a project change, and when the panel is told to focus a

8. **Update fixtures and tests** (`SetupCard.visual-cases.tsx`,
   `SetupCard.test.tsx`, `SetupCard.acceptance.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`,

### Protocol rules

- Every new field is optional. Do not raise the bridge protocol version;
  additive changes use the capabilities list.
- Saved chats written before this change have none of the new fields. The

## Known rough edges. Report them; do not paper over them.

Found by running the formatter over real settings:

- **A zero often means "off" or "automatic".** "Internal solid infill: 0" and
  "0 layers" are accurate and unhelpful. The definitions do not record what
  zero means. Leave these as they are. Do not add per-setting wording.
- **Two settings can share a label and a unit.** "Brim width" is both the
  brim's and the prime tower's. On the setup page the group caption separates
  them ("Others · Brim" against "Multimaterial · Prime tower"). On the card
  there is no caption, so put "page · group · label" in the row's tooltip.
- **Some labels are long.** One is 62 characters. The truncation rule and the
  tooltip handle it.
- **OrcaSlicer's own category field is often empty.** It was blank for 18 of
  33 sampled settings, which is why grouping uses the search index.
- **An object's filament choice.** The `extruder` override holds a slot
  number. Today the card rewrites it as "Filament N · \<preset\>". That is the
  one place a key is named. Either keep that single documented exception or
  show the number; say which you chose.
- **Spiral vase mode** can be set on a plate without being a preset
  difference. Show it in that plate's row on the setup page.

any of them:

2. With no recorded purpose, the title is the process preset and the presets

4. The Plates section shows only each plate's estimate or "Not sliced".

6. The page has no title of its own in the header bar, only "Back".

`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-setup-summary-card/` (2026-10-05)
specified the card that exists now. It stays in force for the title, the
estimate area, attention findings, card states, saved-chat behaviour and its

summary" (the fixed fields) and its inline expandable details.

summary lines and the inline expansion. For those two parts this folder's

Done means all of these, demonstrated and reported with their output:

4. **Saved chats.** A context without the new fields renders with raw values

5. **Guards.** `setting_display_tests`, `workspace_contract_tests`,

6. **Visual check against the mockup.** Add fixture cases for A1, A2 and B to
   `SetupCard.visual-cases.tsx`, render them in light and dark at 320 px, and

   setup page, switch plates, go back. Build `jusprin_web` after every page

be tested, say which and why.

The handoff for the setup summary card is written. It tells another agent to replace the card's fixed list of 13 settings with "which presets are selected and what differs from them", and to move the long details onto a separate page inside the Agent panel. The mockup in it was generated by a script from the design token file and the page's real stylesheet, so no colour, font, radius or size was typed by hand.

## Where it is

The folder is [handoff-setup-card-differences](handoff-setup-card-differences/), untracked, in this session's worktree. Your other handoffs sit in the main checkout, but a safety hook blocks this session from writing there, so you may want to move it.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [README.md](handoff-setup-card-differences/README.md) | The handoff: your decisions, the rules for every line, the styling contract, eight implementation steps, acceptance tests. |
| [mockup.png](handoff-setup-card-differences/mockup.png) | Three screens in light and dark at 320 px, the panel's minimum width. |
| [mockup.html](handoff-setup-card-differences/mockup.html) | The same mockup, inspectable in a browser. |
| [make-mockup.py](handoff-setup-card-differences/make-mockup.py) | The generator. I confirmed it reproduces the mockup byte for byte. |
| [formatter.patch](handoff-setup-card-differences/formatter.patch) | The formatter and its tests from earlier, still uncommitted. I confirmed it applies to a clean checkout of `e3f826a83c`. |

## How the styling is pinned down

- **Existing styles:** the handoff has a table mapping every element in the mockup to the existing `current-setup-*` class it uses, with that class's type role and colour tokens.
- **New styles:** the design adds four CSS rules, all layout or existing variables. No new token is needed.
- **Strings:** every setting value is in the form the tested formatter emits, and the group captions ("Others · Brim") are the real page and group names from OrcaSlicer's settings tabs.

## Changes from the earlier sketch

entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

Access is granted immediately; the session's working directory (for Bash, relative paths, and project settings) moves there when the current turn ends, so use absolute paths until then. `path` is required — the user sees and approves that exact folder (in bypass permissions mode it is granted without asking). Use this when the user's task is about an existing project and the session isn't in it yet; to let the user pick a folder themselves, use request_directory without a path.

path.description: Absolute host path of the folder to move the session to (e.g. ~/code/my-project).

Use this whenever the user asks you to work with files you don't currently have access to.

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

input.title: Fix agent tests broken by approval removal
input.tldr: While finishing the setup card work I found the shared jusprin-newui branch does not compile as committed and 13 agent tests fail on it, all in tool-approval code paths. A new session would fix the build break and bring those tests in line with the approval removal.
input.prompt:
On the JusPrin repository, branch `jusprin-newui` at commit 589563ff99 (which includes f6493ea08b "Remove tool-call approvals that only hurt the user experience"), two problems exist that are unrelated to any feature work:

1. Build break: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, in `make_definitions()`, the `activity_cancel` tool definition ends with `ToolHandler::ActivityCancel, true}`. `struct ToolDefinition` in `ToolRegistry.hpp` has only nine fields (the tenth, an approval flag, was removed), so this does not compile. The fix is to drop the trailing `, true`. (The worktree `~/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin` on branch `codex/setup-card-differences` already carries this one-line fix uncommitted, alongside unrelated setup-card work; do not work in that worktree.)

2. With that fix applied, `agent_bridge_tests` (target `agent_bridge_tests`, binary under `build/arm64/tests/agent/RelWithDebInfo/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/`) reports 13 failing test cases / 22 failing assertions. They are in: `tests/agent/test_mcp_bridge.cpp` (cancellation, malformed cancellation, connection lost, lines ~131-172), `tests/agent/test_mcp_runtime.cpp` (lines ~88-109, ~278-279), `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` (lines ~427, ~1645-1656, ~1800), `tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` (line ~104 `tool["strict"]` expectation, line ~171 printer prompt tool list compared with a JSON file), and `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (test "cancellation and deterministic failure surface over the bridge", section "a native change before execution marks the action stale"). All concern tool states that used to pass through an approval step (pending/running/cancelled/stale) or the tool schema's strictness.

Task: confirm both on a clean checkout of `jusprin-newui`, decide for each failing test whether the test or the code is wrong now that approvals are gone, and fix accordingly. Read `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` first. Build recipe for a fresh worktree: configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib`, then `cmake --build <abs build dir> --config RelWithDebInfo --target agent_bridge_tests`. Do not commit unless asked.

content.text:
The setup card and setup page in the other agent's worktree now match my mockup pixel for pixel, and the real app renders the same design with real presets in light and dark. The largest design mismatch was only visible in the real app: most rows on the setup page had no group caption. Nothing is committed; all changes sit in `/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin` on branch `codex/setup-card-differences`.

## Design mismatches fixed

- **Missing group captions in the real app.** A row read "First layer 50 → 25 mm/s" with nothing to say it was a speed. The lookup the other agent used only knows settings visible in the current user mode. I switched to OrcaSlicer's own table of page and group, which covers every mode.
- **Never checked at the real width.** Its review page drew the card at 405 px with no header. The review page now draws every state at 320 and 429 px, in light and dark, with the page's header.
- **Preset rows capped at 60% width.** Preset and plate rows used the rule meant for change rows, so long preset names would wrap early.
- **Extra spacing wrappers.** The page's markup now follows the mockup's structure exactly.
- **Preset order jumped around.** The page now always lists process, then filament, then printer.
- **Two flaws in my own design**, found with long-text cases: a value could wrap while its label was being cut, and long preset names made the card three lines taller. Both are fixed with one layout rule each.

## Other defects fixed

- **A saved chat's card showed "Agent is applying…".** I found this by restoring the tests the other agent had deleted.
- **About 45 tests and 17 state fixtures had been deleted** for behaviour the handoff said stays unchanged (estimates, working, out of date, saved cards, attention). They are restored and adapted.
- **The "nothing was read" and "no agent" cards had been changed** to claim "No changes from presets" or offer a link. Both are back to a plain preset label.
- **The chat's change log showed raw tokens** ("auto_brim → outer_only") right under a card saying "Auto → Outer brim only". The log now records readable values.
- **The guard against hard-coded settings checked only five names.** It now reads every setting from OrcaSlicer's definitions, and I confirmed it fails when a setting name is added to the card.
- **Agent attribution could survive a preset switch** when nothing was edited at the time of the switch.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Pixel comparison with the mockup (6 frames) | Identical, apart from the focus ring on "Back" |
| Page tests (`npm test`) | 412 pass |
| Formatter, workspace contract, theme and brand guards | Pass |
| Real app, new `--setup-differences-capture` harness mode, light and dark | 88 checks pass |
| Other harness runs (default, timeline, recomputing) and the real-adapter program | Pass (527, 99, 76, 972 checks) |
| Agent bridge tests | 13 cases fail |

The 13 failures also occurred before I changed anything, in files this work does not touch, and all concern tool approval states. The shared branch also does not compile as committed; the other agent's one-line fix for that is still in the diff. I did not build the base branch to confirm the failures there, so "pre-existing" is my conclusion, not a measurement. I flagged a separate task for it.

## Decisions for you

- **The setup page header has only "Back".** That matches the mockup, but it means the pane's collapse button is not reachable from that page. Say if you want it added.
- **The chat timeline's one-line agent summary still names three settings by label** ("N walls", infill density and pattern). That is the same hard-coded-fields pattern, in a component outside this handoff. I left it alone apart from keeping its wording lower case.
- **Commit.** Say the word and I will commit this on the branch.

In the evidence image, "card=Setup" in the message box is the harness's probe text, not an app defect.

content.text:
Yes, you were right about the live run, and all three things are now done: the collapse button is on the setup page, the real app has been captured in the mockup's actual state, and the hard-coded chat timeline summary is gone. Everything is still uncommitted in `/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin`.

## The live run did not match the mockup

My earlier "real app" picture showed a different state from the mockup, and I put it beside the mockup without saying so:

- **No purpose was recorded**, so the title was the preset name ("0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C"), not "Stop the corners lifting".
- **Because the title was the preset**, the line under it showed only the filament.
- **All edits were made by hand**, so the two rows were whichever I edited last (a printer retraction setting and bed temperature).
- **Nothing was sliced**, so there was no estimate.

The run now records a purpose and applies the changes through the same tools the agent calls, slices the plate, and waits out the one-minute "Updated" state. The third image shows the result next to the mockup: purpose as title, "0.20mm Standard · Bambu PLA Basic", two of the agent's changes, the count line, the estimate. 108 checks pass in that run.

That run exposed one real defect, now fixed: when the agent changed several settings in one go, the card picked its two rows in reverse log order, which is arbitrary. Settings changed together now keep OrcaSlicer's own order, the same order as the "just changed" line.

## The chat timeline summary

This is the one-line pill the chat shows when the agent makes a change with two or more settings. The first image shows the problem:

- **It searched for three settings by name**: "Wall loops", "Sparse infill density" and the infill pattern. For a strength change it read "Laid flat · 5 walls · 35% gyroid +3".
- **For any other change it named nothing.** A bed-adhesion turn (brim type, brim width, first layer speed) read only "Add modifier: Corner tab +1".
- **The "+1" was wrong.** It assumed two settings had been named, so three changed settings were reported as one more.

It now shows the step name and an exact count ("Laid flat   6 settings"), with every setting listed when opened. The bottom half of the first image is an interim version that could truncate the count; the second image is the final form, where the count cannot be cut. The other option was to name the first two settings, but that does not fit on one line at the panel's narrow width.

## Collapse button

The setup page header now has "Back" on the left and the panel's hide button on the right, as the chat header does. The real-app run clicks it and checks the panel hides.

## Verification

- 415 page tests pass.
- The real-app run passes all 108 checks, and the harness's timeline capture passes all 82.
- Against the mockup, the card and page body are still pixel-identical; the header differs by the new button and the focus ring on "Back".

## Decisions for you

- **The card's lead row can be an ambiguous label.** In the real run it reads "First layer  50 → 25 mm/s", because OrcaSlicer labels the setting "First layer" inside a group called "First layer speed". On the setup page the caption resolves it; on the card only the tooltip does. I recommend showing "group · label" on the card whenever OrcaSlicer gives the same label to more than one setting. Say if you want it.
- **Figma is now out of date in two places**: the "Agent change summary" frame still shows "5 walls · 35% gyroid +3", and the setup card frames still show the old summary and inline expansion.

content.text:
Yes, it is intended, but your question shows it is not clear enough. "+2" means the project has two more filament slots besides the first one, here three in total: Generic ABS plus two Generic PLA. The card names only the first to keep the line short.

Two problems with it as written:

- **"+2" does not say two of what.** It can read as part of the filament's name.
- **It counts configured slots, not filaments the objects on the plate use.** Your calibration object may print in ABS only, and the line would still say "+2".

It also partly repeats the header, where the filament chip already shows three colour dots next to "Generic ABS".

My recommendation is to spell it out: "0.20mm Standard · Generic ABS and 2 more". It costs seven characters, and a line that runs long already ends in an ellipsis, with the full names on the setup page.

The alternative is "0.20mm Standard · 3 filaments", which is shorter and unambiguous but drops the filament's name from the card.

Tell me which you prefer and I will change it. Counting only the filaments the plate actually uses is a separate, larger change, because the app does not send that to the card today.

input.command:
git remote get-url origin && git switch -c temp/setup-card-differences && git add resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin tests/agent tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp tests/workspace && git status --short | grep -v "^[AM] " ; git diff --cached --stat | tail -1 && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Show differences from presets on the setup card, with a setup page

The setup summary card in the Agent panel described a print with a fixed
list of 13 slicer settings, so it could not show any other setting and
showed wall loops to someone asking about bed adhesion. It now shows the
selected presets and what differs from them, by one rule that covers every
setting. The long details move to a setup page that replaces the chat body,
so the card never grows.

Card: title (the chat's recorded purpose, else the process preset), the
process and first filament preset cut at " @", the first two differences
with a count of the rest and of objects with overrides, then the estimate
as before. Differences the agent made come first, newest first; settings
changed in one go keep OrcaSlicer's order.

Setup page: presets in full, differences grouped by preset and by the page
and group each setting has in OrcaSlicer's settings tabs, per-object
overrides, and each plate's estimate. Back and the panel's hide button are
in its header. It has no message box.

App side:
- SettingDisplay.hpp formats any setting's value from its own type, unit
  and choice labels; no setting key is named in it.
- Differences are sent for the process, filament and printer presets, each
  with its formatted change and its page and group. The page and group
  come from the table every option group registers in, not from the search
  index of options visible in the current user mode.
- The change log records a setting's values as a person reads them, and
  each entry carries the setting's key.
- kSetupKeys and the applied-settings array it filled are removed.

Chat timeline: the one-line summary of an agent change looked up three
settings by label and named nothing for any other change. It now shows the
step and an exact count, with every setting behind it.

Tests: the card's behaviour tests and state fixtures are kept and adapted;
a guard reads every setting from PrintConfig.cpp and fails if the card or
page source names one; the shell harness gains --setup-differences-capture,
which edits real presets, applies a patch through the agent's tools, and
checks and photographs the card and the page.

Also drops a stray argument in the activity_cancel tool definition that
stopped ToolRegistry.cpp compiling after the approval removal.

Known: 13 agent_bridge_tests cases fail, all in tool-approval code paths
this change does not touch.
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short | wc -l
